item.title: Between Burning Forests and Utopian Cities: Designing the Climate Transition
item.dc:creator: Olivia Poston
item.description: There is no shortage of ways to imagine what the world will look like after a climate catastrophe. Genres of movies and novels have been built around the question of what happens when contemporary safeguards fail, from dystopian fiction and post-apocalyptic literature to disaster films, graphic novels, and video games. Burning forests, submerged cities, abandoned infrastructure, resource scarcity, and mass displacement are a familiar visual and narrative vocabulary. We have become remarkably fluent in imagining the consequences of a world that fails to respond to climate change.

item.title: Casa Estelí / COLAR Colectivo de Arquitectura
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: The project is based on a critical and conscious look at the act of building, understanding architecture not as an isolated object, but as a cultural, environmental, and social process deeply linked to the territory and the community that inhabits it. From this perspective, the intervention proposes the conservation and transformation of built heritage as an essential strategy to extend the life of buildings, recognizing the tangible and intangible value they contain. Reclaiming an existing structure does not imply freezing it in time; rather, it means reinterpreting it, allowing it to incorporate new layers of meaning and use, and ensuring it continues to be an active part of the place's evolution.

item.title: Architecture on Water: What Living at Sea Can Teach Us About Space and Materials
item.dc:creator: Kiana Buchberger
item.description: Unlike buildings, which are anchored to foundations and respond to climate from a fixed position, yachts are designed for constant movement and change. Interiors sway with the vessel, light changes by the minute, humidity is a permanent design condition, and every kilogram influences performance. Designing for the sea therefore requires architects, naval architects, engineers, and interior designers to solve questions that rarely exist on land: how can space remain calm while everything around it is in motion?

item.title: BIG’s Macondo Park Opens as a Temporary Cultural Landscape for Shakira’s Madrid Residency
item.dc:creator: Reyyan Dogan
item.description: Following the opening weekend of Shakira's Madrid residency, Macondo Park has officially opened at the Iberdrola Music venue in Villaverde, Madrid. Designed by Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG) in collaboration with Komodo and Vampire, the 185,000-square-meter temporary destination surrounds the venue designed by BIG for Shakira's concerts, extending the venue with a series of cultural and public spaces inspired by the fictional town of Macondo from Gabriel García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude. The park will host daily cultural programming alongside the concerts throughout the singer's 12-show residency, which continues through October 11, before its temporary structures and landscape elements are dismantled and removed from the site.

item.title: Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus / Feilden Clegg Bradley Studios
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus (TQEC) is the most significant development in the recent history of the University of Bristol and a major new civic landmark for the city. The project transforms the long-derelict former Royal Mail sorting office site beside Brunel's Grade I-listed Temple Meads station into a new center for learning, research and innovation and civic engagement, redefining one of Bristol's most prominent gateways.

item.title: Google Unveils New Renderings of Chicago's Thompson Center Redesign, Marking Its Escape From Demolition
item.dc:creator: Antonia Piñeiro
item.description: On September 16, 2026, Google announced the redevelopment of Chicago's Thompson Center as a space for work, culture, and community. The James R. Thompson Center is a postmodern architectural landmark designed by Helmut Jahn and completed in 1985. Commissioned by Illinois Governor James R. Thompson, the building reinterprets the classical state capitol by turning the traditional dome-and-public-plaza concept inside out. Occupying an entire city block in Chicago's Loop, it features a multicolored, curved glass atrium and a sloping, transparent corner entry. Controversial from day one, it has been criticized for poor climate control, high maintenance costs, and structural and leak issues. To restore it rather than demolish it, the company collaborated with Architecture Plus Information (A+I) to design a project that would integrate the building into the urban life of Chicago's Loop.

item.title: Designing Domes in the Digital Age: From Concept to Preliminary Estimate
item.dc:creator: Agustina Iñiguez
item.description: Despite being among architecture's oldest structural forms, domes continue to offer possibilities for creating large, column-free spaces and working with circular or free-form geometries beyond conventional rectangular building types. Their evolution has been closely tied to changes in materials, construction methods, and design tools. Today, digital platforms are adding another layer to this process, allowing some of the decisions traditionally developed later in a project to be explored much earlier.

item.title: Above the Snowline: 11 Shelters Built at the Limits of Construction
item.dc:creator: Diogo Borges Ferreira
item.description: There is no harder place to build than a high mountain, and none where a building feels more provisional. From the Andes to the Himalaya to the Alps, high-altitude construction strips architecture back to its most elementary transactions. The rock reads as permanence itself, yet a structure set near the limit of habitation exists in negotiation with almost everything around it: with wind that arrives without obstruction, with a ground too steep and too frozen to excavate, and with everything it needs arriving from far below. What can be carried up, what can be assembled by few hands, and what can sustain itself are some of the terms of the problem.

item.title: Common Nexus University / Tetsuo Kobori Architects
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: The Tokai National Higher Education and Research System envisioned Common Nexus (ComoNe) as a commons of knowledge and innovation—a place for making and fostering connections between the university and the community, among people, and between the past and future. Our team was selected for the project through a competitive call for proposals held in 2021.

item.title: TH+ house / ODDO architects
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Woven into the dense urban fabric of Hanoi, TH+ House occupies an extremely constrained plot just 2.5 metres wide, accessible only through a network of narrow pedestrian alleys and surrounded by the city's characteristic informal vertical houses. In Hanoi's alley neighbourhoods, density is not only a physical condition but also a social one. Shared tea, small businesses, children playing in the street, and spontaneous encounters create a strong sense of community within an otherwise highly compressed environment. This social intensity became an important premise for the design of TH+ House.

item.title: HEYTEA Craft Store / say architects
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: No one wants to wait for a cup of tea. Scan, pay, wait for your number, take it away. The cup is warm, but how the tea came to be is nowhere to be seen. New tea beverages have pushed everything toward speed: faster launches, faster service, faster replication of the next store. A hit is outdated before it is even remembered. HEYTEA Craft Store wants to do something else: to slow down.

item.title: Casa PM / Feliu Vega Kennedy Arquitectura
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: The project is located on an 8,600-square-foot lot in the warm valley of Challuabamba, in a privileged location characterized by wide views of the northern mountains and a small ravine to the east.

item.title: MRD Residence / Jacobsen Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Pilar Caballero
item.description: Next to a dense tropical forest located in the outskirts of São Paulo, the MRD House project sought to adapt to an uneven terrain through solutions that focused on creating paths and viewpoints to the surrounding nature.

item.title: Casa Amona / COLAR Colectivo de Arquitectura
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: The project is located on an urban lot in San Cristóbal de las Casas, adjacent to one of the city's main green areas. The house maintains a restrained relationship with the street, focusing its daily life toward the interior of the property, where various openings and courtyards establish visual connections with both the surrounding landscape and the home's internal spaces.

item.title: CASA ÂNCORA / Tiago Sousa
item.dc:creator: Andreas Luco
item.description: A remote, rugged and serene place, marked by the contrast between heat and cold.

item.title: Ellen Browning Building / Hacker Architects
item.dc:creator: Andreas Luco
item.description: The genesis for the mixed-use residential Ellen Browning Building arose when a group of close friends considered how they could preserve their relationships during their last years. Co-housing, with its spirit of community and shared living spaces, provided the answer. By developing their own residential building, the friends would be able to balance togetherness with the independence of urban living. The site they selected is set within a vibrant retail and commercial district along Division Street in Southeast Portland. Like many seniors, choosing to live in a walkable, amenity-supported and health-care rich city is an aging-in-place strategy.

item.title: The Gallery House / Maden Architects
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: "The Gallery" is conceived as a contemporary residence where architecture, natural light, movement, and landscape come together to create a calm and refined living experience. The project is inspired by the idea of architecture as a continuous journey rather than a collection of separate spaces. Clean geometric volumes establish a strong architectural identity, while carefully framed openings, courtyards, and landscaped areas create a constant visual and spatial relationship between the interior and its natural surroundings.

item.title: The Forum Installation 2027 Open Call for Site-Responsive Installations
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
The Forum at Fabrik invites students and emerging designers to propose a temporary spatial installation for a prominent public-facing site in the Gaslight District, one of Cambridge's emerging cultural and urban destinations.

Created to support the next generation of designers, the program provides an opportunity to take an idea beyond drawings and models—to design, build, and present a full-scale work within an active public setting.

Up to three proposals will be selected and realized sequentially over the course of one year. Each selected project will receive:

Up to $4,500 CAD in project support to realize the installation
A $500 CAD honorarium through The FORUM

item.title: Call for Abstracts: 2027 Modern Conversation Conference on Education
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Join our upcoming annual edition of “modern conversations”, where we examine spaces of pedagogy to analyze the shifting terrains of educational practices, institutions, and environments that influence the creation and dissemination of knowledge. This inquiry prompts us to consider: where does learning occur, both historically and in the contemporary world? What is the connection between modernity and education? In what ways has modernity transformed educational spaces? When did education adopt a formal structure, and how was this reflected spatially? How have socio-political dynamics shaped these environments? Most crucially, why is it critical to examine the spaces where education happens?

item.title: Open Call: Urban design competition for the Kłodnica Boulevards in Gliwice
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: The City of Gliwice invites entries for a one-stage urban planning, landscape, and architectural design competition to develop a development concept for the Kłodnica Boulevards in Gliwice. The goal of the competition is to obtain a high-quality urban planning, landscape, and architectural concept for the Kłodnica River valley within the city limits of Gliwice. We are seeking visionary solutions that will transform the riverside corridor into a vibrant, multifunctional public space, integrate urban green spaces into a cohesive natural system, create safe walking and biking routes, and strengthen the city’s resilience to climate change.

item.title: Oris Day
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
The Oris Day architectural symposium takes place on Sunday, 8 November 2026, in Zagreb, at the Mozaik Event Centre.
The central programme will bring together this year’s Pritzker Prize laureate Smiljan Radić Clarke and Swiss architect Christian Kerez. The audience will have the opportunity to follow their conversation live – a dialogue between two distinguished architects about architecture, the creative process and contemporary challenges facing the profession.

item.title: RE_SOLUTION: Fernando Medina, former Mayor of Lisbon, at IE School of Architecture & Design
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
IE School of Architecture & Design (IE University) will launch the 2026–27 edition of its RE_SOLUTION public series with a lecture by Fernando Medina, Mayor of Lisbon from 2015 to 2021, followed by a conversation with Jo da Silva, Global Director of Sustainable Development at Arup.

RE_SOLUTION brings together former city leaders and experts to examine how cities respond to complex urban challenges through public infrastructure, transformative projects, policy, and collaboration across government, the private sector, academia, and civil society.

item.title: Festival des Architectures Vives
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Festival des Architectures Vives 2027 in Montpellier: Call for Applications

The Festival des Architectures Vives (FAV) has launched its call for applications for its 21st edition, taking place in Montpellier, France, from 15 to 20 June 2027. Under the theme “Shared Happiness”, the festival invites young professionals in architecture, landscape architecture, urban planning and related disciplines to design temporary installations for the historic courtyards of Montpellier’s private mansions.

Applications are open until 7 December 2026.

item.title: Anthology ASEAN Architecture Festival
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Anthology ASEAN Architecture Festival 2026: Shared Ground
Architecture of Care, Culture, and Collective Futures
October 2–4, 2026 · Intramuros, Manila, Philippines

I. Leading ASEAN Voices in Architecture is coming to Intramuros for Shared Ground

Ground, in Southeast Asia, has never been neutral. It bends under monsoon rain, shifts with reclaimed coastlines, and carries the layered memory of settlements, colonial grids, and postwar cities built one on top of another. This is the premise the Anthology ASEAN Architecture Festival 2026 opens with: that the terrain our region builds on is shared, climatically, historically, and socially, whether we choose to acknowledge it or not.
